votes.reasoning: All four scanners now take their windows from CostWindow(now:). The call sites are ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:56-58, CodexSessionScanner.swift:97-99, CodexLogScanner.swift:32-34 and OpencodeScanner.swift:126-128. A grep of Sources finds no remaining 7*86_400 window cutoff in the scanners. The window is today plus six prior local days, built with Calendar.date(byAdding:) (CostWindow.swift:30), so it stays calendar-aligned through DST and is safe under the per-day memo. Reversal check: I put back the old -7d and rolling cutoffs and the seven_day_window_boundary tests went RED in all four scanners (Claude 15 vs 5, Codex 30 vs 10, CodexLog 3.75 vs 1.25, opencode 100 vs 10). Token semantics are untouched: Codex still does input-cached with reasoning folded into output, and opencode still keeps input as-is with reasoning added to output.

The four scanners had four separate boundary computations. They now share one definition, Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cost/CostWindow.swift:269-281, used at ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:114, CodexSessionScanner.swift:185, CodexLogScanner.swift:143 and OpencodeScanner.swift:293. It steps by calendar day with Calendar.date(byAdding:), not raw 86_400-second steps. The `??` fallback is not a swallowed error: date(byAdding:.day) on a valid date only returns nil in theory. CostWindow is a new Core file, and it gets its own test file, CostWindowTests.swift (window span plus DST), as CLAUDE.md §4 requires. Each scanner test asserts one fact at a time with non-Bool comparisons, which the Testing policy allows. The README was updated in the same change. Nesting and function size are unchanged.

The new Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cost/CostWindow.swift:21-32 is now the only definition of the 7-day window, and all four cost sources use it: ClaudeSessionScanner.swift:56-58, CodexSessionScanner.swift:97-99, OpencodeScanner.swift:126-128 and CodexLogScanner.swift:32-34. Touching the legacy CodexLogScanner is in scope. It is still live as the fallback in CodexCost.swift:31, and its figure feeds the same summed 7-day total, so leaving it on the old now-7*86400 cutoff would have left the mismatch the finding describes. The new public CostWindow type is a Sendable value type with no persistence. It has its own tests (CostWindowTests), so it meets the new-file-needs-a-test rule. README.md:30 now describes the window. The 86_400 values left in AnalyticsAggregator.swift:76-89 belong to history analytics windows, not the cost windows, so they are a separate thing and not a missed sibling route.
